overall_judgment.recommended_action: Retain the primary FY2025 net financial cash and correctly rounded CFO ratios. Optional one-clause clarifications for relative valuation and gross-margin comparability are sufficient; a new paid-review cycle is not justified by these findings. Continue to characterize the decision as conditional on the adopted required-return framework, as the memo already does.

That is a cash-paid/profit ratio, not a measured unlevered operating tax rate: settlement timing and nonoperating items differ. The full provision-to-cash reconciliation is not modeled.
The $34.588 billion cash payment also exceeds the $27.062 billion income-tax provision by $7.526 billion; the packet does not allocate that difference to specific settlements or timing effects.
The 17% preference uses the latest expense-rate structure and quarterly guide as a forward anchor, not an assumption that the $7.526 billion cash gap reverses.
Tax-law, earnings-mix and settlement changes can still raise cash burdens: the 20%/24% operating-tax tests give base values of $156.17/$148.30, as well as the weighted values below.
House decision at the snapshot quote: pass on initiating under the adopted approximately 10% required-return framework.
